title: EPF Work Package Schema
description: A work package is the bounded, non-permanent execution unit that binds stable strategy (Value Model L1-L3, Definitions, Key Results) into a scoped statement of work with a clear outcome and bounded time. It is the tool-agnostic, four-track HANDOVER CONTRACT between strategy authoring and downstream execution substrates (coding agents, strategy-as-code, ecosystem partners). It is deliberately THIN: it declares outcome + targets via references, and each execution substrate decomposes it its own way. Tasks, scheduling, and collision detection are intentionally out of scope - they belong to the execution substrate and orchestrator, not to this schema.
$comment: WORK PACKAGE ARCHITECTURE: EPF models stable strategy at L1-L3 (Value Model -> Definitions -> Key Results). The work package fills the gap between that stable strategy and disposable execution. DESIGN PRINCIPLES: (1) Thin binding - a work package REFERENCES value model paths, definition ids, and KR ids; it never copies their content. (2) Four-track aware - a single work package may advance multiple tracks. (3) Many-to-many targets - a WP advances multiple KRs and a KR spans multiple WPs (1:1 was rejected because WPs would grow too large and KRs too numerous to stay meaningful). (4) Non-permanent - a WP is time-boxed and disposable, with an explicit lifecycle and a 'cancelled' terminal state honoring the 'not forever' property. (5) Substrate-agnostic - no task model; execution substrates own decomposition. TWO ORIGINS: A work package can originate on either side of the strategy/implementation boundary. (a) EPF-authored (source.authoring_tool = custom | partner-native): written in EPF before execution as a statement-of-work handover, typically for org-ops, commercial and partner work. (b) Implementation-authored (source.authoring_tool = openspec): written in the code repository, where product and code work only splits into work packages once the implementation spec exists, then mirrored one way into EPF and treated as read-only there; source.reference points to the tracker item (e.g. an issue URL). Execution detail (estimates, tasks, repos, PRs) stays in the tracker in both cases. HISTORICAL NOTE: An earlier 'work_packages' concept (removed in EPF v1.9.6) was a THICK task/ticket object that duplicated Linear/Jira. This schema is intentionally different: it is a binding CONTRACT, not a ticket. CONVENTIONS: This schema BORROWS conventions from track_definition_base_schema.json (four-track enum, status lifecycle) and shares its value-model path pattern with feature_definition_schema.json via definitions/value_model_path but does NOT extend it - a work package is an execution INSTANCE, not a procedural definition with maturity tiers. FOOTPRINT: A WP's footprint (the collision key used by orchestrators to compute parallel-safe waves) is the union of value_model_paths + definition_ids it touches. The footprint is DERIVED server-side from targets, never authored here, so it cannot be under-declared. This schema only models the targets. additionalProperties is set to false to keep the contract thin and prevent accidental task/scheduling fields from leaking in.

value_model_path.description: A Value Model path: {Track}.{Segment}.{Segment}[.{Segment}] - three or four dot-separated segments. Track is Title case (Product|Strategy|OrgOps|Commercial). Segments accept either the display-name form ('Product.Core Platform.csv-import') or the PascalCase form ('Product.CorePlatform.CsvImport'), so paths copied between feature definitions, track definitions and work packages all validate.
value_model_path.$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE PATTERN: this definition is duplicated verbatim in work_package_schema.json and feature_definition_schema.json (kept local, not a cross-file $ref, so each schema stays loadable on its own). validate-schemas.sh fails if the two copies diverge. Edit both together. It is a superset of the previous work_package and feature_definition patterns, so existing artifacts remain valid.

id.description: Unique work package identifier. Format: 'wp-{number}' with at least three zero-padded digits. Unlike track definitions (which use per-track prefixes fd/sd/pd/cd), work packages use a single cross-track 'wp-' prefix BY DESIGN - a work package can span multiple tracks, so a per-track prefix would be misleading. IDs are immutable (never reuse, even after a WP is done or cancelled).

title.description: Human-readable name describing the work package's outcome. Title case, outcome-oriented. Good: 'CSV Import Hardening', 'Enterprise SSO Onboarding'. Avoid generic activity phrasing like 'Do the import work'.

intent.description: The outcome this work package commits to deliver, stated as a bounded result, not a task list. Answers: what will be true when this WP is done? Should be verifiable and substrate-agnostic (no implementation steps - those belong to the execution substrate).
intent.$comment: Keep intent focused on OUTCOME, not activity. The WP is a contract about what changes, not how it gets built. If you find yourself listing steps, that is a sign the content belongs in the execution substrate's decomposition, not here.
examples: CSV import succeeds for files up to 100MB with clear, recoverable errors, so that onboarding no longer stalls on data import.
Enterprise customers can authenticate via SAML SSO with self-serve configuration, removing the manual setup bottleneck.

track.description: The primary EPF track this work package belongs to. A WP may TARGET value across multiple tracks (see targets), but it has one primary track for ownership and routing. Mirrors the four-track model used across EPF (product, strategy, org_ops, commercial).
track.$comment: The primary track determines default ownership and which value model the WP is most associated with. Cross-track value is expressed through targets.value_model_paths, which can reference any track's value model.

targets.description: What this work package advances. All three target arrays are MANY-TO-MANY: a WP advances multiple KRs and a KR spans multiple WPs. The union of value_model_paths + definition_ids forms the WP's footprint (derived server-side), used as the four-track collision key for computing parallel-safe execution waves. This schema only models the targets - it does not author the footprint.
targets.$comment: Targets are pure references into existing strategy artifacts. Relationship validation (each reference resolves to an existing value-model path / definition id / KR id) is enforced by validate-work-package-references.sh, not by this schema (JSON Schema cannot do cross-artifact resolution). At least one of the three arrays should be non-empty in practice; empty arrays are permitted at the schema level to support staged authoring (e.g. a 'proposed' WP whose targets are still being resolved).

value_model_paths.description: Value Model L1.L2.L3 paths this work package advances. Format: {Track}.{Segment}.{Segment}[.{Segment}] - 3 or 4 segments, identical to feature_definition 'strategic_context.contributes_to', so paths can be copied from a feature definition unchanged. Track segment is Title case (Product|Strategy|OrgOps|Commercial). Segments may be display names ('Core Platform', 'csv-import') or PascalCase ('CorePlatform', 'CsvImport'). May span multiple tracks. Part of the footprint collision key.

definition_ids.description: Track definition ids this work package operates against. Uses the canonical per-track definition id format: fd-* (product/feature), sd-* (strategy), pd-* (org_ops/process), cd-* (commercial). Part of the footprint collision key.

kr_ids.description: Key Result ids this work package advances. Uses the canonical roadmap KR id format kr-{p|s|o|c}-{number}. Many-to-many: a WP may advance several KRs and a KR may be advanced by several WPs. NOT part of the footprint (footprint is value_model_paths + definition_ids only).

risk_class.description: Risk classification that drives downstream review rigor (e.g. a Tier-3 strict/auto review gate in the execution substrate). low = routine, auto-reviewable; medium = needs human review; high = needs strict review and explicit sign-off. This schema only declares the class; enforcement lives downstream.
risk_class.$comment: risk_class is an authoring-time declaration of how much scrutiny the work needs. The orchestrator/execution substrate maps risk_class to its own review policy - this schema does not encode review behavior.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Normal flow: proposed -> approved -> scheduled -> executing -> done. 'cancelled' is a terminal state reachable from any non-terminal state, honoring the 'not forever' property of work packages (mirrors Shape-Up's 'rejected'). The status state-machine (allowed transitions, side effects, journal events) is enforced downstream in strategy-server; this schema only constrains the set of valid values. Tools that mirror a work package from an implementation tracker (source.authoring_tool = openspec) must not move its status backward along the normal flow; status only advances (or becomes cancelled).
status.$comment: TERMINAL STATES: done and cancelled. 'scheduled' records that the WP has been placed into an execution wave; the actual scheduling/collision logic lives in the orchestrator, not here. This schema deliberately does not model transitions - it only validates the value.

source.description: Authoring-tool provenance. Records where this work package was authored so downstream consumers can attribute and route appropriately.

authoring_tool.description: Which kind of tool authored this WP, and therefore where it originates. openspec = implementation-authored: written in the code repository via an OpenSpec-style spec flow and mirrored one way into EPF, read-only there; custom = EPF-authored directly (manual/wizard); partner-native = EPF-side handover of work authored in an ecosystem partner's native tooling.
authoring_tool.$comment: This enum is intentionally generic and product-neutral per CANONICAL_PURITY_RULES.md - it names CATEGORIES of authoring tool, not specific products or organizations.

reference.description: Optional pointer back to the authoring artifact (e.g. a spec id, or the URL of the tracker item the work package is mirrored from). Free-form; not resolved by EPF.

lifecycle.description: Time-boxing metadata. A work package is non-permanent: it is created at a point in time and is expected to close. This captures the 'not eternal' property.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this work package was created.

target_close.description: Optional target date by which this work package should reach a terminal state (done or cancelled). Expresses the time-box. Omit only if the close date is genuinely unknown at authoring time.

closed_at.description: Optional ISO 8601 timestamp when this work package reached a terminal state. Set by the execution substrate when status becomes done or cancelled.
